text:
ops-oncall: Getting multiple customer p95/p99 complaints in us-south started ~2026-03-17T16:12:00Z. Spike concentrated on TLS handshake timeouts and 20-40% increase in SYN->TLS RTT. Grafana: ingress->egress path shows a jump at 16:11. :eyes:
Maya: Thanks — is this only us-south? any DNS or GSLB changes?
Ajay: Checked GSLB weight change logs: no config pushes in the last 24h. No deploys.
Olivia: Customer support shared traces: majority of failed requests show TLS 1.3 server handshake timeout between 150-400ms, compared to baseline 30-60ms.
sre-bot: Alert: route-flap-detector fired on us-south-egress (count: 18) at 2026-03-17T16:10:54Z.
network-eng: We're seeing a small but sharp increase in RTT to a subset of upstream peering in us-south. Could be congestion on one peering link. BGP counters show transient AS path change to PeerX for ~2m.
Maya: Can we reproduce from our probe fleet? ask probes for tcpdump/traceroute to affected origin IPs.
Ajay: Running quick probe: `for i in 1..5; do traceroute -T -p 443 origin.example.com; done` — traces show an extra cross-az hop for some probes (us-south-a -> us-south-b -> upstream-peers).
Olivia: Support: impacted customers are mostly high-connection-rate APIs. They see p99 tokenization calls spike.
ops-oncall: Action list: 1) collect tcpdumps on edge host 2) reweight GSLB if peering looks bad 3) temporarily steer traffic to us-east if needed.
Maya: tcpdump snippets (sanitized):
```
16:12:05.123456 IP 10.10.1.1.443 > 192.168.2.2.54321: Flags [S], seq 0
16:12:05.223789 IP 10.10.1.1.443 > 192.168.2.2.54321: Flags [S], ack 1
```
Shows SYN retransmit and delayed TLS client hello.
network-eng: Confirmed: our eBPF packet counters show queueing at peer interface on us-south-b. Latency spike correlates with 1 of 3 peer uplinks reaching 85% util.
Ajay: Is this driven by customer traffic or internal backfill? Any large batch jobs?
Olivia: No internal batch in last hour per job-scheduler. Seems customer traffic + a transient reroute caused concentration on one uplink.
Maya: Mitigation plan: 1) reweight GSLB away from affected POP (temporary) 2) push BGP community to prefer alternate peer for high-priority routes 3) increase local egress queue length threshold while we shift (short-lived).
ops-oncall: I'll start reweight in 1m. Will notify if rollback needed.
network-eng: FYI, pushing route to alt-peer now for routes with community 0xBEEF. Expect propagation within 30s.
Maya: After reweight, p95 on TLS handshake reduced from 310ms -> 68ms within ~45s. p99 still a hair above baseline (~120ms) but trending down.
Olivia: Support to customers: "We routed around a congested peering link in us-south which reduced TLS handshake latency. We're monitoring and will follow up when root cause confirmed."
ops-oncall: Keeping temporary BGP preference for 10m, then will evaluate. Captured pcaps and traceroutes attached to the incident ticket.
Ajay: Postmortem notes to collect: - time window 16:10-16:15Z - affected POP: us-south-b - root cause candidate: transient peering uplink congestion + AS-path shift - mitigations executed: GSLB reweight and BGP community steering - observable impact: p95 TLS handshake down by ~78% within 1m
network-eng: We'll open a ticket with PeerX to request logs for the 16:10-16:15 window and ask for congestion explanation.
Maya: Quick check: no auth or billing errors in traces — purely transport layer.
sre-bot: Incident annotated: severity=sev2, ticket=INC-20260317-142.
ops-oncall: Will keep thread updated. If p99 climbs again, plan B is to fail traffic to secondary region (us-east) and kick a canary autoscale for capacity.
Olivia: Customer-facing follow-up drafted.
Maya: Adding repro steps for postmortem: 1) run synthetic probe hitting same origin from edge in us-south 2) capture `tcpdump -i eth0 port 443` and `sudo tcptraceroute -T -p 443` 3) correlate with BGP feed: `bgpctl show adj` 4) check peer counters on net-metrics.
ops-oncall: Resolved for now — metrics stable 5m after actions. Closing monitoring window but leaving ticket open until peer response. :white_check_mark:
